question: Can the original native-prefix executor support matched repeated futures that distinguish high-load action-cost instability from prediction error?
basis: The fixed matched-pair contrast is HOLD. Higher-cost errors dominate despite more improved than worsened changed actions. Label instability is an untested hypothesis, not a finding.
work: Trace which future randomness can actually change after an identical native prefix, given fixed route arrivals, SUMO random state and the current executor.
Determine how to preserve checkpoint traffic state, candidate identities, PP continuation and paired randomness across actions; do not assume snapshot restoration is valid.
If feasible, propose one small fixed label-repeatability protocol with independent future units and an explicit budget; otherwise document why the proposed repeat does not identify label instability.
scope: Design and existing-code/artifact audit only. Do not tune objective, weights, features, thresholds, folds or leaf size; do not launch collection or closed-loop expansion.
reason: Broader evidence review prioritizes native source-target data compatibility and direct transfer; future-label randomness is retained only as a conditional hypothesis.
